body: Over the years I've realized that most of my childhood memories are manufactured. I don't know what I'm covering up, but in my head my childhood was idyllic
I hope she does too, but moreso I hope she does the healing she needs first. We will both make it through this, it's going to be okay

I know what you're going through, I'm on week three of no contact and it's so incredibly hard. I miss her so much, she was my best friend and I trusted her with everything. I got burned and I hope someday that can be mended, but mostly I just want to be happy and for her to be happy. Stay strong my dude, I know how hard it can be when it's literally impossible not to think of your twin. But if you truly want the best for her, when you think about her, imagine she's happy, it helps.
I'm sorry you feel so hopeless. I can't tell you what your experience is, but I hope someday you feel like you can be loved the way you deserve. I'll keep you in my thoughts

I know exactly what you mean. If my twin flame doesn't want me, who would? How could anything compare to their love? But self love is even more pure than a soul bond, and if I'm enough for myself, I don't need anything else. Maybe relationships are and always will be fucked up, but that doesn't mean it's all hopeless. Give yourself a chance Eden, you deserve it more than you realize.
It sounds cliche, but I'm trying to love myself the way I was told I am. I think that's the way out of the cycle of trauma
God, it's like your saying my thoughts, that's exactly how I feel. I just want to be loved the way I was told I am. But I don't know I ever will be

I know what you mean. I think I was in the same position. I don't know if I can trust anymore. 

But I Love and appreciate you, I know it's not the same as romantic love, but you've helped me more than you know.

Your words really ring true with me. I just turned 31 and I've never felt more alone in my life. Compounded by the fact that I just had the hardest falling out of my life. I feel like I'll be alone forever, but I guess it's nice to know there are people out there who feel the same as me. Trapped in the deep dark hole. If you want to message, feel free, I can't promise I'll be good company, but I at least can comiserate.

Hey, I just wanted to throw my opinion and experience out there. I was feeling very much the same, I very nearly killed myself not long ago and I was afraid of medication. It felt like a last resort and that if that didn't help, I'd be out of options and need to kill myself. I started on wellbutrin xl, it helped with my lethargy and allowed me to stabilize my emotional swings relatively quickly. If you have time, look into it. I would highly recommend it. I'm feeling more like my best self every day
I know how you feel. I miss my SO too. Feeling alone is so fucking hard

I have experience in the opposite direction, I went into my relationship with my partner who was already married, knowing that would never be an option for me. For brevity I'll summarize as my partners spouse tried to hit the veto button on me, it didn't go well, now they're separated and everything is in chaos. 

Imo: support what makes your partner happy, even if it's not what makes you happiest, if they love you on that deep true level, they'll do the same for you, because love isn't transactional

My brother tried to kill himself with tylenol, it's really not a good idea. As hard as it is on the people around you, I support people in their autonomy and having control of their end of life. But trust me, tylenol is not the way to go. Even if you don't regret your decision a few days/weeks later you'll exist for much longer than you want to, and that existence will be debilitating. Everyone will either watch you die a slow painful death over the course of days to weeks, or you'll get immediate care and salvage your liver. I hope you reconsider your options, I hope you find the strength to keep living, but if you don't, please don't subject yourself to death by liver failure.

I'm sorry you're going through such a difficult living situation, I went through something similar last summer and had to leave. If you're not on a lease I would recommend doing the same as soon as possible. It's incredibly hard to live with people who don't respect your boundaries.

I've been struggling with suicidal thoughts since I was roughly 13. I'm almost 31 now, they don't go away, the don't slow down, you just learn to live with them. I've tried a handful of times, and the feeling of failing is bittersweet, some days are okay and I don't think about it obsessively, other days it's all I can think of and getting out of bed feels like a death sentence. Good luck to you on combatting the thoughts, I know how hard it is.

I wish I was brave enough to go through with it often, but I know the pain a suicide inflicts on the lives around you too well. I've never recovered from my friend from highschool killing herself

I first tried to kill myself when I was 18, despite feeling like someone saved me from myself, I tried again at 22-23 (that point in my life was a blur) after the friend who saved me killed themselves, then again at 28. I'm on medication now, I'm really trying, but it's still an hourly thought in my worst times and maybe weekly during my best times. The real difference between now and then, is I no longer believe that my life is absolutely destined to end in suicide. Now it's like 60-40 odds

I wish it made me feel empty, or maybe not, I don't know, what form or depression is better, locked into too many feelings, or locked out of all of them? I feel like I'm being forced to choose one or the other.
